ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors and authorized signatories against UN Consolidated Lists, EU Financial Sanctions Databases, OFAC SDN List, and Spanish national lists as published by SEPBLAC/BOE; enhanced due diligence for PEPs identified under Ley 10/2010 and SEPBLAC guidance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central – Denominaciones Sociales (online via Colegio de Registradores: https://www.registradores.org)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Spanish or any other official language of the European Union; non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin characters. The name must be unique in the Central Registry, not conflict with existing names, and must include the Spanish suffix 'Sociedad Limitada (SL)' or 'SL'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within one month of the rejection notification, the applicant may file a recurso de alzada before the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado (DGRN) via the Registro Mercantil Central, attaching the negative certificate and written legal grounds; alternatively, a new name application for a different denomination may be submitted immediately.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this technology SaaS industry if the virtual office provides a physical street address in Spain (not merely a post-office box) and administrative/mail handling services; however, the registered office must remain consistent with the actual place of management under Art. 9 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (below 5% annual likelihood) for unannounced on-site inspections in the absence of regulated licensure, government subsidies, or public procurement exposure.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC), Articles 20-22 (incorporation), 58-60 (minimum capital), 62 (registered office), 209-210 (administration).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) for name certification; Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry) for final registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (Deed of Incorporation) and accompanying application for registration (Inscripción en el Registro Mercantil).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital for Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) is EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid up in cash or in-kind at incorporation. No escrow account is required; capital must be deposited in a Spanish bank account and evidenced by a bank certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the company be incorporated as a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada under the laws of Spain. That the share capital of EUR 3,000 be subscribed and fully paid in by the founding members. That the registered office be established at Calle de Alcalá 45, Madrid, Spain. That the following officers are appointed: [Name] as Managing Director and [Name] as Secretary. That the company engage in the business of bulk transactional email API and newsletter hosting services. That the board is authorized to execute all documents and take all actions necessary to register the company with the Registro Mercantil and obtain the NIF.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Certification (Certificado Negativo de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) – online via CIRCE system or in person.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name application with three proposed company names in order of preference. The registry issues a negative certificate confirming no identical or confusingly similar name exists. The certificate is valid for 3 months.
required_dossiers: Completed application form (Solicitud de Certificación Negativa)
Copy of applicant's ID or passport
Payment of the official fee (approx. EUR 15)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a new application with alternative names. If the certificate expires, reapply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation (Escritura de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Notario) in the jurisdiction of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the deed of incorporation including the articles of association (estatutos), capital structure, and officer appointments. All founding members must appear before the notary with valid identification. The notary verifies the legal capacity and the bank certificate of capital deposit. The deed is signed and notarized.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate of capital deposit (Certificado de Depósito)
Passports or ID of all founding members
NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) for non-resident members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects, correct the deed and resubmit. If a member is absent, arrange for a power of attorney.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Capital Transfer Tax and Stamp Duty (ITP/AJD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Tributaria (Spanish Tax Agency) – provincial office or online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of notarization, file the deed with the tax agency and pay the 1% capital transfer tax (Modalidad de Operaciones Societarias) on the nominal capital. Obtain the tax payment receipt (Modelo 600).
required_dossiers: NIF of the company (provisional if not yet obtained)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax payment is delayed, interest and surcharges apply. File a corrective declaration if errors are found.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Provisional NIF (Código de Identificación Fiscal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Tributaria – local tax office or online via CIRCE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized deed and tax payment receipt to obtain a provisional NIF (tax identification number). This number is used for all subsequent filings. The provisional NIF is valid for 6 months until the final NIF is issued after registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is incomplete, the tax agency will request additional documents. Provide them within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial corresponding to the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized deed, tax payment receipt, and provisional NIF with the provincial registry. The registry reviews the deed for legal compliance and issues the registration certificate. This step legally completes the incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registry fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry raises objections (defectos), correct the deed or provide additional documentation. The registry will issue a note of defects (nota de calificación) and allow a 2-month cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Final NIF and Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Tributaria and Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, return to the tax agency to exchange the provisional NIF for the definitive NIF. Register the company and its directors with the social security system (TGSS) for employer and employee obligations.
required_dossiers: Registration certificate from the Commercial Registry
Directors' NIE and social security numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NIF is not finalized, the provisional NIF remains valid. For social security, ensure all directors are registered to avoid penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – the business is a digital service provider (ISIC 6201) and does not require industrial licensing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no specific operating license is required for email infrastructure SaaS under Spanish law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable – no physical operations or emissions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the activity is purely digital and does not trigger EIA requirements under Ley 21/2013 de Evaluación Ambiental.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – no wastewater, VOC, or waste handling. However, if a physical office is leased, the landlord must ensure compliance with municipal building codes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: If a physical office is established, a municipal occupancy license (licencia de actividad) may be required from the local ayuntamiento. Fire safety certification (certificado de protección contra incendios) and structural load inspections are required for commercial premises. For a purely remote digital company, these are not applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Madrid. Electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es); corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades), VAT (IVA) and withholding filings are conducted via the e-Sede using an electronic certificate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Non-resident founders first obtain an NIE (foreigner identity number); the founding notary requires a provisional company NIF issued on Form 036. 2) Execute the incorporation deed before a notary and inscribe the SL in the Registro Mercantil. 3) File census Form 036 within 1 month of incorporation to obtain the definitive NIF (letter B plus 8 digits) and to register for IS, IVA and employee/service-provider withholding obligations. 4) Obtain an electronic certificate (FNMT digital certificate or Cl@ve PIN) to access AEAT online services and the OSS/SII schemes where applicable. Non-resident suppliers without a Spanish fixed establishment may register directly for VAT via Form 036 or the EU One Stop Shop (OSS) and appoint a tax representative only where law requires.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The SL is a resident capital company taxed on worldwide income under Ley 27/2014 (LIS) at the general 25% rate; no pass-through of profits or losses to shareholders. Distributions to non-resident shareholders are subject to dividend withholding at 19% (subject to treaty relief). Territorial scope is worldwide, with credit for foreign taxes attributable to foreign permanent establishments; special regimes of the Basque Country, Navarra and the Canary Islands are not applicable to this common-territory entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spanish law has no check-the-box classification election; the SL is a corporation by mandatory statute. Available statutory options: (i) fiscal consolidation group election (Arts. 64-75 LIS) for an SL joining a group with ≥75% (or ≥70% if listed) parent shareholding; (ii) reduced 15% IS rate for newly created SLs in the first 2 tax periods with a positive tax base and actual business activity (Art. 29.3 LIS); (iii) SME relief (empresa de reducida dimensión, net turnover < EUR 10 million): reduced rate of 23% on the first EUR 300,000 of taxable base and 25% on the excess; (iv) patent-box and R&D/innovation tax credit elections under LIS; (v) hybrid mismatch and CFC rules (Art. 15 quater LIS implementing ATAD I/II) apply mandatorily, with no domestic election to opt out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido) under Ley 37/1992, harmonised with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; administered by AEAT. Canary Islands (IGIC), Ceuta and Melilla (IPSI) are outside the EU VAT area.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 for the resident SL: VAT registration is compulsory from the first taxable transaction regardless of turnover (Form 036). For distance sales of goods and B2C digital/electronic services (e.g., newsletter subscriptions) to consumers in other EU Member States, the OSS regime applies with a EUR 10,000 annual intra-EU threshold; above this threshold, Spanish VAT is chargeable by reference to the customer's Member State rates and declared via OSS. Non-established suppliers have no general exemption threshold in Spain.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) real-time invoice-record filing to AEAT applies to large taxpayers with turnover exceeding EUR 6 million and to VAT groups; a standard email-infrastructure SL below this threshold files periodic VAT summaries (Modelos 303/390) without per-invoice clearance. No digital stamping or pre-clearance exists for ordinary export invoices. B2B structured e-invoicing will become mandatory under Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) once its implementing regulation is approved, using Facturae/XML-compatible interoperable platforms; RD 1007/2023 (Verifactu) imposes certified software/hash-invoice standards for invoice-issuing software, phasing in from December 2024. All invoices must comply with RD 1619/2012 (mandatory fields, serial numbering, issuer and customer VAT identification).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports to non-EU destinations are zero-rated (0%) under Art. 21 LIVA on proof of physical exit from EU customs territory. Intra-EU dispatches are exempt under Art. 25 LIVA with the customer's valid operator VAT number (NIF-IVA) and Intrastat filing where applicable. Cross-border services (B2B email API and newsletter hosting supplied to business recipients established outside Spain, whether inside or outside the EU) are not subject to Spanish VAT under the general place-of-supply rules of Arts. 69-70 LIVA, with reverse charge applicable at the customer's jurisdiction; B2C digital supplies to non-EU consumers are also not subject. To substantiate zero-rating the SL must obtain and retain evidence of the customer's establishment and business status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA/SAD filed through the EU AES/ECS system, with MRN status EXA)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR evidencing physical exit from EU customs territory
Commercial invoice compliant with RD 1619/2012 including supplier and customer VAT identification
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT or PSP payment confirmation linking the export transaction to incoming foreign currency
Customer's foreign VAT/GST registration certificate or equivalent proof of business establishment for reverse-charge or OSS treatment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under Ley 58/2003 (LGT), AEAT may claw back refunds and zero-rated amounts for up to 4 years, plus statutory late-payment interest (interés de demora), and impose graduated penalties: 50% for material omissions or under-declarations and up to 150% for concealment or fraudulent evasion, with penalties on undue refunds calculated on the full amount obtained. Repeated and patterned fraudulent export claims may constitute organised fraud and trigger Criminal Code Art. 305 liability where the defrauded amount in one tax period exceeds EUR 120,000, punishable by 1-5 years' imprisonment and fines of up to 6 times the defrauded amount. Export records must be retained for at least 4 years (recommended 6 years) from the filing deadline.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting within the Eurosystem of the European Central Bank (ECB); foreign investment statistical and screening registrations are administered by the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores of the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (Secretaría de Estado de Comercio, Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. Spain maintains no generalised exchange control regime; EU Treaty free-movement-of-capital provisions (Articles 63–66 TFEU) guarantee unrestricted profit remittance and capital injection for EU counterparties. For non-EU investors, no prior exchange-control authorisation is required, but post-transaction statistical reporting applies: inward direct investments exceeding EUR 1,000,000 per act (or investments in certain regulated/sensitive sectors regardless of amount) must be filed with the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores within 30 days of the transaction. Dividend and royalty outbound remittances are free of forex restrictions; the only substantive hurdles are domestic withholding tax (19% dividend WHT under the general rate, 24% for non-cooperative jurisdictions unless treaty relief is available) and the anti-tax-haven / CFC substance rules. For profit repatriation to a non-EU shareholder, documentary proof of economic substance (payroll, premises, operational invoices in Spain) is essential to avoid AEAT recognition as a shell-flow. Currency convertibility for the existing banking account will be automatic via Banco de España operational clearing; no surrender or prior deposit requirement applies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters must retain invoicing in any freely convertible currency and may hold proceeds in foreign currency. However, a mandatory statistical reporting duty applies to Banco de España's Balance of Payments regime: any individual cross-border transaction exceeding EUR 50,000 (or EUR 12,500 in cash) must be declared by the resident exporter via the D-2 statistical declaration form (or through the electronic declarations service of the Banco de España). The declaration is only informative/statistical, not an authorisation, and it must cover the settlement of export invoices within the 6-month general valuation window established by the Spanish Commercial Code and IFRS 15 revenue recognition of export service earnings. Late filing of the statistical declaration may trigger penalties up to EUR 6,000 for first-time negligence; deliberate concealment can trigger AML scrutiny under Law 10/2010.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.additional_notes: As the entity operates a low-risk SaaS (ISIC 6201) in EUR, no FX conversion permit is required for subscription receivables from Latin American or European clients; only the D-2 reporting at the EUR 50,000 threshold must be embedded in treasury operations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium — European Monetary Institutions (EMIs) licensed in the EEA (e.g., Wise Europe, Revolut Business, Airwallex, multitudes of Spanish EMI licensees) may passport into Spain under PSD2 and obtain indirect access to the SEPA and SWIFT rails without opening a local branch. They are viable for daily operational receivables and multi-currency vendor payments at materially lower fees than Tier-1 Spanish banks. However, they exhibit three binding constraints: (i) EMIs cannot grant credit or hold regulated deposits as principal, so they are not suitable for long-term treasury escrow or for the initial risk-capital tranche; (ii) some EMIs are not participants in the Spanish instant-payment RCE/SPEI, creating T+1 clearing gaps; and (iii) AEAT and Banco de España de-prioritise EMIs for VAT refund offsets and for validation of foreign tax credit certificates. A hybrid architecture is recommended: Tier-1 Spanish bank for capital, tax payments, and dividend remittances; one EEA EMI for daily Stripe Billing sweeps and Latin American FX settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid regime. Since entry into force of Royal Decree-Act 7/2021 for the transposition of AMLD5 and the Banco de España Circular 2/2018, Spanish banks have adopted mandatory face-to-face or live video-identification for non-resident directors of newly incorporated SLs. In practice, Tier-1 banks (Santander, BBVA, CaixaBank) will require at least one physical presence in Spain by the managing director for the initial signature-taking; remote opening is allowed only if the signatory has previously appeared before a Spanish notary and holds an authenticated notarial power of attorney, and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) must undergo a supervised video interview with the bank's compliance team. For a fully remote model with no physical director, Spanish corporate law requires the appointment of a resident legal representative (persona física or gestoría) with a general power of attorney to open the account; banks commonly reject accounts with no Spanish nexus if turnover is projected to exceed EUR 500,000 p.a. without that resident anchor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial paid-in capital funded via intercompany loan from a non-EU parent in a jurisdiction classified as 'high-risk' or 'non-cooperative' by FATF (e.g., certain jurisdictions in Latin America or non-EEA jurisdictions).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the escritura de constitución; certificate of registry filing (certificado del Registro Mercantil); the executed intercompany loan agreement with arm's-length interest and repayment schedule; bank reference letter from the lender's home-country bank (SWIFT KYC); certified proof of source of funds for the lending bank; and a sworn declaration of the UBO of the lender confirming absence of shell status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared ISIC 6201 email-infrastructure purpose and the actual inbound wire pattern (large batch payments from multiple Latin American merchants, suggesting alternatively payment-processing or crypto-adjacent flows).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed enterprise subscription agreements with named counterparties; Stripe Billing settlement reports matched to VAT invoices issued in Spain (invoice series in aedea format); server/lease and data-residency contracts with the hosting provider; monthly transaction ledger showing that each inbound SWIFT corresponds to an invoiced subscription period; and a written AML self-assessment demonstrating that the platform does not control or custody client funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unduly low paid-in capital under the SL 'minimum capital requirement: false' fallback (i.e., a EUR 1–3,000 share capital) combined with unusually high projected turnover in the first year (EUR >1 million), which is a canonical shell-indicator profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan with cost build-up and hiring forecast; board resolution approving a capital increase to an amount commensurate with the first 12 months of opex; proof of professional indemnity/cybersecurity insurance; a reference letter from a correspondent bank of the foreign parent; and the notarised declaration by the Spanish resident agent that the company is operational from the registered office.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO resides in a high-risk third-country without any commercial nexus to Spain, while the entity holds the Spanish NIF and the Spanish mailbox is virtual.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled notarial identification of the UBO; proof of physical office lease in Spain (not a virtual office) with at least one work seat; appointment of a resident managing director with ordinary powers; the three-month operating evidence (rent, salary, social security contributions) subsequent to opening; and a substance memorandum demonstrating strategic and operational management located in Spain (EU functional-substance rule).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.onboarding_documentation_master_list: CIF/NIF certificate for the company; Certificado de apoderado for each signatory; Escritura de Constitución / Estatutos; Registro Mercantil certificate; Spanish tax payment calendar; UBO declaration (form 08/2018 recommended); certificate of non-residence for foreign directors; and a bank-provided risk questionnaire for ISIC 6201 commercial activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant routing for the initial equity injection and subsequent paid-in capital from a non-EU shareholder is as follows: (1) The sole/shareholders must provide funds via bank credit transfer (SWIFT MT103 with settlement on the Spanish IBAN) using the euro; the bank's remittance instructions must include the company's BIC/IBAN and a purpose memo stating 'equity contribution – capital increase of ES_SL'. (2) In the SWIFT /ISO20022 purpose field, the transfer should carry category purpose code 'EQUI' (equity investment) or, where the bank uses Balance-of-Payments functional classification, the code for direct investment equity capital (FDI-equity). (3) The documentation bundle for the receiving bank will include the notarised deed of capital increase and the Registro Mercantil entry certificate. (4) For any single inward equity instalment exceeding EUR 1,000,000 originating from outside the EU/EEA, the entity must file the 'Declaración posterior de inversión extranjera' with the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores within 30 days (Form DP-1/DP-2). (5) For a capital injection sourced from an intra-group treasury hub in the EEA, the reporting threshold is relaxed to EUR 10,000,000 under the EU statistical regime, but the D-2 declaration to Banco de España still applies at EUR 50,000. Verification requires proof of the final beneficial ownership chain and the absence of co-mingling with the entity's operational subscriptions. Transfers arriving in non-EUR currency must be converted on arrival through the receiving bank's FX desk; alternative conversion through a fintech EMI (e.g., Wise for the USD leg) is permissible but should be segregated in treasury records for audit trail completeness.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For an email-infrastructure SaaS, the outbound disbursement rails are categorised as follows: (i) European Economic Area (EEA) invoices from hosting, CRM, and infrastructure suppliers (e.g., cloud data-centre leases, software licences): SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and, for time-critical renewals, SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) with IBAN-to-IBAN settlement; these are cleared through TARGET Instant Payment Settlement (TIPS) or PB-SCT within 10 seconds at negligible cost. (ii) Non-EEA trade settlements to cloud providers (e.g., US AWS or GCP consolidated invoices): SWIFT MT103 (telegraphic transfer) with full beneficiary bank identification; for recurring subscription SaaS payments, an open-account model with the supplier's XeroStripe billing is standard and commercially effective. (iii) Intercompany royalty and management-fee disbursements to the foreign parent: SWIFT MT103 with automatic submission of the Spanish Corporate Income Tax clearance certificate to avoid WHT leakage, plus the D-2 statistical declaration when above EUR 50,000. (iv) Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary collection L/C at sight) are permitted under Spanish banking law and are used only when the Latin American enterprise client requires the supplier to post a performance standby L/C (SBLC) for the platform service; these are rare in pure SaaS and, given the service's intangible nature, a confirmed irrevocable SBLC with SWIFT MT799 pre-advice and MT750 application may be accepted. For recurring third-party newsletter infrastructure clients, standard trade terms remain open-account with payment on Stripe Billing/recurring card and monthly MT103 reconciliation. The treasury must monitor cut-off times of the correspondent bank (Banco de España window closes at 16:00 CE(S)T) to avoid overnight float.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD foreign exchange forwards (deliverable) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Spanish/EU bank or EU broker-dealer, available with 1-, 3-, 6-, and 12-month tenors, used to cover USD-denominated enterprise subscriptions and AWS/GCP invoices.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted Latin American and emerging currencies (ARS, NGN, EGP, and USD/offshore variants), triangulated to EUR, with settlement in EUR and valuation based on the prevailing Banco de España reference rate; available from Tier-1 banks with credit lines for SLs.

EUR/USD cross-currency swaps (CCS) where the entity has a material fixed-rate USD liability or a long-dated invoice-finance obligation; the swap converts principal and coupon flows to EUR and is transacted under the same ISDA/CSA framework.

European-style FX options (call to buy EUR / sell USD; put to protect the receivable) used as premium-earning instruments when the entity's Latin American clients pay in USD with a lag of 60–120 days; commercial banks price volume-based vanilla options and will require an ISDA tariff.

Upgradeable NDF/forward laddering with a semi-annual roll — a customised treasury overlay: sequential 1-month forwards that hedge the rolling AR balance of the Brazilian merchant settlement, subject to the bank's agreed outstanding-hedge notional limit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.liquidity_manager_architecture: The treasury blueprint instructs a dual-rail liquidity manager: (a) the Tier-1 Spanish bank acts as the settlement bank of record, holding the operating account, paying AEAT (taxes) and treasury services, and processing dividend remittances; (b) an EEA-licensed EMI aggregates day-to-day subscription sweep from Stripe Billing and executes FX conversions for Latin American currency inflows, flowing residual EUR back to the Tier-1 account daily via SCT. This avoids daily SWIFT fragmentation and allows the treasury desk to carry only the minimum EU funding buffer in the EMI. All balances must be reconciled using a 3-column cash-flow chart (receivable, payable, and capital) and an intraday sweep order reminder aligned with EBA clearing windows to avoid intraday settlement risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Depósito de Cuentas Anuales (Annual Financial Statements Deposit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil of the company's registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual accounts must be approved by the Junta General within six months of the fiscal year-end and deposited within one month of approval; for a calendar-year company, the effective filing deadline is no later than 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure (cierre registral): the registry sheet is marked as closed and no instrument may be registered until accounts are filed; the Instituto de Contabilidad y Auditoría de Cuentas may fine the company up to EUR 10,000; failure to deposit accounts for three consecutive fiscal years allows the registrar to presume inactivity, initiate compulsory dissolution, and ultimately remove the company from the registry (administrative strike-off).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Modelo 200 (Corporate Income Tax Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the corporate tax year; for a calendar-year taxpayer, the filing deadline is no later than 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharges of 5%, 10%, 15% or 20% depending on delay plus late-payment interest; failure to file triggers a fixed penalty of EUR 200 per return plus EUR 20 for each EUR 6,000 of tax base; substantial valuation or documentation irregularities may attract penalties from EUR 600 to EUR 15,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalización de Libros Registro (Annual Legalization of Statutory and Accounting Books)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil (Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública) through the EnviarLibro electronic platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Legalization of each electronic book must be submitted within four months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, the legalization window closes on 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Infringement of Article 26 of the Código de Comercio punishable by fines of EUR 1,200 to EUR 6,000; unlegalized books are denied evidentiary weight in judicial and administrative proceedings and the company sheet remains subject to registry closure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registro de Titulares Reales – Annual UBO Confirmation and Post-Share-Transfer Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: UBO status is confirmed annually in the declaration embedded in the deposit of annual accounts; each share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days from the notation in the Libro Registro de Socios.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Classified as a serious/pre-serious money-laundering offence under Ley 10/2010: fines of EUR 60,000 for the company and up to EUR 5,000 for negligent officers; suspension of shareholder voting rights may result until the UBO record is restored; no administrative strike-off is imposed solely for UBO non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Modelo 390 – Resumen Anual de IVA (Annual VAT Summary Declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 30 January following the close of the previous calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Assessed default may be subject to late-payment surcharges of 5%/10%/15%/20% plus interest; failure to file the annual summary is penalized with EUR 200 per outstanding obligation plus EUR 10 per data block, and continued non-compliance may trigger forced tax assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Modelo 347 – Declaración Anual de Operaciones con Terceras Personas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 28 February (or 1 March in leap years) for transactions carried out in the preceding calendar year; filing is compulsory where aggregate annual transactions with a single counterparty exceed EUR 3,005.06.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing carries a base penalty of EUR 200 plus EUR 10 for each data set; omission of substantial information may be penalized under Article 198 of the Ley General Tributaria and, for intentional concealment, penalties are graduated from 50% to 100% of the concealed amount.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must appoint a registered auditor (auditor de cuentas) if it meets at least two of the following thresholds on two consecutive balance-sheet dates: (i) total assets exceed EUR 4,000,000; (ii) annual net turnover exceeds EUR 8,000,000; (iii) average number of employees exceeds 50. Audit is also mandatory for parent companies that must prepare consolidated accounts and for any entity operating in regulated financial or investment sectors, irrespective of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Plan General de Contabilidad approved by Real Decreto 1514/2007, which is the Spanish accounting framework harmonized with EU accounting directives; small entities apply the PGC de PYMES under Real Decreto 1515/2007; consolidated financial statements are prepared under EU-adopted IFRS in accordance with Real Decreto 1159/2010.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Real Decreto 304/2014 and Ley 10/2010, every transfer of participaciones must first be entered in the Libro Registro de Socios; the company is then obliged to file the updated beneficial ownership statement in the Registro de Titulares Reales within 30 days of such notation. Annually, the company confirms its UBO data through the specific declaration included in the deposit of annual accounts; in all cases, the registered data must reflect the substantive beneficial owner, including any natural person holding more than 25% or ultimately controlling the entity, and any non-compliance with annual confirmation or transfer updates exposes the company to fines of up to EUR 60,000.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Administradores – when required by minute book notations)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $150–$800 per annum for registered-office domiciliation and compliance-agent services in Spanish commercial cities
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,500–$12,000 per annum for a small or mid-sized email-infrastructure SL, excluding VAT

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
